distinguishing_features: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) generates cavitation micro-bubbles as transient heterogeneous nucleation sites in supercooled water.
Deterministic acoustic pressure threshold (P_ac >= 5 MPa) triggers ice nucleation independent of stochastic supercooling fluctuations.
Integration of HIFU transducer array into cloud seeding payload, replacing passive dispersal nozzles.
Operation at marginal supercooling (-3°C) where passive silver iodide seeding is inefficient.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reliably initiate ice nucleation in supercooled cloud droplets at marginal supercooling temperatures where passive seeding is inefficient.
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism is physically feasible because high-intensity focused ultrasound can achieve the required 5-10 MPa peak negative pressure to generate cavitation bubbles that act as heterogeneous nucleation sites, and the proposed bench-scale test is implementable with standard HIFU equipment.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The use of acoustic cavitation to deterministically trigger ice nucleation in supercooled water is a distinct mechanism from the prior art, which are in unrelated fields (flotation, polysilicon fouling, carbonylation) and do not suggest applying HIFU to cloud seeding.
